Skeptical protocol review — round 1
29 September 2026. Independent review of pulsechain_dai_feasibility_20260928.md (main paper) before
receiving the other reviews' findings. Scope: contract composition, identity, bridge accounting, Portal
and the difference between inherited, observed and hypothetical configurations. Read-only source and
saved-evidence inspection; no new public transactions, administrative actions or modified-fork
experiments. The review does not evaluate the previously excluded Origin/Morpho-specific route.
Verdict
The strongest defensible affirmative result is conditional architectural coherence: a transferable
source receipt can be held in bridge custody while its authorized destination representation is exchanged
for an existing local asset. The underlying can remain invested. A separately funded local exchange can
then buy pDAI. Historical reverse-gateway source supplies real mechanics for the custody and mint
steps.
The paper does not establish a complete deployed source-to-pDAI path at its pinned snapshot. It also
does not establish that validator control, token-unit balances and administrative control produce enough
economic buying power. Its explicit conditions generally acknowledge this. Nevertheless, the abstract
and conclusion can be read as stronger than the evidence because they join component demonstrations
to a separately funded AMM example. Their connection is an assumed funding and integration edge, not
an observed or fully constructed end-to-end witness.
The revised thesis is consequently narrower than the original proposition. It has not shown that
apparently unbacked copied balances become dollar-equivalent collateral by being attested, deposited
and wrapped. It has shown that investment claims can be transported and financed if those claims
receive usable financing or market demand. This narrower statement is meaningful, but the change in
proposition should be explicit.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 371

Evidence directly inspected
Historical L1ReverseCustomGateway.sol and L2ReverseCustomGateway.sol, saved under artifacts/parb-
historical-bridge-models-20260929/, pinned to commit 64cfba62f6dc1ce3b89869db341956f298810299. The
function bodies support L2 custody and L1 bridgeMint; the misleading historical header comment
should not override those bodies. Pinned L1 source.
The saved explorer source for the deployed Aave V3 implementation, artifacts/parb-debt-
history-20260929/v3_implementation_source.json. Its BridgeLogic calls validateSupply, enforces the unbacked
cap, increments unbacked and mints the local aT oken. Settlement reduces unbacked and transfers
the actual reserve underlying to its aT oken contract. Explorer source.
Saved reserve summary artifacts/parb-loop-accounting-20260929/reserve_summary.json: DAI/USDC/USDT
cash, unbacked and unbacked caps are zero; DAI and USDT aT oken supplies exceed their configured
supply caps. These are observations at block 27,659,393, not observations of every later state.
The wrapper inventory, Portal accounting, historical bridge and Reserve collateral studies cited by
the main paper. These establish specific identities and limitations; this review did not independently
repeat their chain calls.
ERC-4626: shares implement ERC-20, but nontransferable implementations are permitted.
Conversion views describe idealized accounting; withdrawal limits and actual execution are
separate. Its ordinary mint receives assets and does not constitute unrestricted bridge mint authority.
Strongest support
The reverse-gateway source is a genuine pre-fork architecture, not an invented modern bridge
feature. The L2 gateway measures the increase in its token balance after custody transfer, while the
L1 override invokes the paired token's mint method.
Existing ARB and GRT destination mints, as documented in the audit, refute a universal claim that
every destination delivery must come from pre-existing L1 escrow. They do not establish source
backing or universal token compatibility.
The exact V3 aT oken/wrapper relationship supplies a coherent local Portal-to-wrapper interface.
Portal's receipt can be an ordinary local aT oken; it need not be a newly named remote
representation. This is distinct from the generic reverse-gateway path.
An existing Reserve issuer can issue the exact token already listed in its Curve pool. That avoids the
mistaken assumption that a bridged receipt itself must equal the pool coin. It still requires the actual
active basket and valuation conditions to accept and receive the correct assets.
Nothing in these mechanisms logically requires the source investment to be sold merely because its
transferable receipt enters escrow. The bridge can transport ownership of a claim without moving
the underlying investment.
Ranked corrections and additions
Critical: define the proposition without assuming its conclusion
Split the result into three statements: historical interfaces exist; a specified hypothetical composition is
internally consistent; sufficient purchasing assets can move a specified market to a target. Do not
describe the third as proving the second's financing. Section 2's assumption of actual purchasing
liquidity currently bears almost the whole economic burden.
A defensible theorem should identify initial holders and end holders of each asset, the actual financing
asset, each exact interface, required cash and residual obligations. It need not claim a historical
execution. Until that witness exists, use “architecture outline” or “conditional composition,” not a proof
of a complete deployed route.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 372

Critical: distinguish three meanings of backing
Add explicit definitions:
Token-unit custody backing: destination claims correspond to source receipts under bridge
accounting.
Source protocol solvency: the receipts can realize the claimed underlying under that protocol's
obligations and withdrawal rules.
Economic purchasing capacity: a counterparty or funded market provides an executable quantity
of local assets for the claims.
The first does not establish the second or third. A trillion source units may be completely escrowed while
receiving no financing. Source validators accepting an invented balance can establish neither
independent economic demand nor realizable investments merely through acceptance. Even real source
receipt units can face losses, unavailable redemptions or a market discount. This distinction strengthens
the paper without requiring Ethereum dollar redemption.
High: qualify conservation for asynchronous execution
The main paper's simple settled one-to-one model is reasonable, but its companion states D = E too
generally. Between source lock and destination mint, escrow exceeds minted representations; between
destination burn and source release, it also remains committed while the redemption is pending. For
fixed units and no donations or losses, a useful accounting relation is:
committed escrow = outstanding destination representations + pending issuance rights + pending redemption rights.
This is a schematic accounting identity, not a claim those rights are all directly enumerable in the
existing contracts. Include finalized-message processing, duplicate-message exclusion, cancellation rules
and other destinations when applicable. Timing can change who has an enforceable claim without
changing total collateral.
High: describe the reverse lifecycle
A convincing invested-receipt model needs more than entry. Describe which destination claim is
surrendered on return, how the source receipt is released, and how that receipt can subsequently
redeem underlying. Account for source withdrawal queues, frozen tokens, transferable ownership and
share-rate changes. Otherwise “backed” can be mistaken for immediately redeemable.
For static shares, bridge the share count and leave the source conversion rate as a separate quantity. Do
not assume destination collateral plugins automatically know the current rate or underlying liquidity. A
functioning oracle reports a valuation; it does not deliver assets.
High: surface the independent Aave barriers
Main text mentions zero Portal caps but omits a second material observed barrier: DAI and USDT aT oken
supplies already exceed their configured supply caps. The deployed Portal path calls validateSupply, so
enabling only an unbacked cap would not establish issuance availability. Also preserve role, reserve,
amount and wrapper-transfer conditions. A V2 wrapper is not a V3 Portal wrapper.
The main Portal inequality is sound as a principal cash-flow condition. It should remain explicitly
conditional on successful swaps and actual backing transfers. Ordinary repayment does not close the
unbacked balance, and cash obtained by a wrapper sale is not retained treasury cash after being used to
back that issuance.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 373

High: bound administrative hypotheticals
Separate (a) already inherited exact configuration, (b) existing functionality under changed parameters,
and (c) new adapters or changed implementation behavior. A new representation accepted by a new
market is not proof that the old pools accept it. Full arbitrary code control would make a very broad
existence claim nearly trivial; the useful theorem should restrict itself to named accounting models and
compatible interfaces.
Medium: make rejection conditions readable
Add a compact route checklist: exact source unit; custody or burn operation; authorized destination
issuer; exact output token; accepted market/collateral identity; funding asset and amount; settlement;
return/redemption. Mark each as observed, historical source behavior, hypothetical or unresolved. Any
broken edge blocks that particular composition, not every architecture in the paper.
Also replace the conclusion's awkward “selected the account as their plan” with “adopted this
mechanism as their plan.”
Counterexamples and falsifiers
Accepted state, worthless receipt: all bridge permissions and custody are valid, but no lender or
buyer provides local purchasing assets. The broad validator-to-$1 sufficiency claim fails while the
custody bridge works correctly.
Correct symbol, wrong token: a representation called aDAI reaches L1, but the Balancer wrapper
accepts only its configured local Aave aT oken. The proposed direct deposit fails; a separate
integration would be needed.
Empty ordinary gateway: accepted withdrawal plus zero escrow produces no ordinary stablecoin
delivery. ARB/GRT-specific mint authority does not fix this token's transfer path.
Portal cap enabled, supply check fails: the independent DAI/USDT supply-cap condition blocks
fresh issuance at otherwise unchanged sampled state.
Local issuer recognizes a token only in its registry: the active basket still requires other exact
assets. Registration alone does not establish issuance from the new receipt.
Receipt sale at a discount: wrapper proceeds are smaller than new Portal principal plus fees.
Repetition accumulates an obligation unless another asset funds it.
Bridge completes, buying budget too small: all contract transitions succeed but the funded
output fails to move the stated market and trade size to the target.
A live receipt-to-pDAI route would require all its specified predicates simultaneously. A failing example
falsifies a universal claim of sufficiency; it does not disprove an existential claim allowing different
funding and integrations. A theorem so permissive that every failed predicate may simply be assumed
away would have little explanatory power.
Independent confidence judgments
These are subjective ranges for the stated propositions, not calibrated frequencies, future-price forecasts
or probabilities that an undisclosed network exists. They should not be multiplied across reviews sharing
evidence.

for the target

under selling and redemption

H2 and H4 are judgments about what the paper establishes, not assertions that no such route or future
price could exist. This review did not separately recompute every numerical digit of the AMM example.
H1's high confidence is partly a consequence of its explicit funding and acceptance conditions; it should
not be quoted as confidence in the original unconditional thesis.
Round 1 is complete. Awaiting shared findings before round 2.
